data.title: Atropine sulphate injection
data.summary: VI Emergency drugs · Antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) belladonna alkaloid
data.body:
_Injectables · VI Emergency drugs_

**Class:** Antimuscarinic (anticholinergic) belladonna alkaloid

## Mechanism of action
- Competitively blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
- Heart: blocks vagal tone → raises heart rate and AV conduction
- Also reduces secretions, relaxes smooth muscle, dilates pupils

## Pharmacokinetics
- IV onset within 1 min; IM within 15 min; half-life about 2–4 h

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Symptomatic bradycardia — including severe vasovagal reaction during dermatological procedures
- Organophosphate/carbamate insecticide poisoning (large repeated doses)
- Pre-anaesthetic to dry secretions; reversal of neuromuscular block (with neostigmine)

## Dose & formulations
- Bradycardia: 0.5–0.6 mg IV every 3–5 min, up to a total of 3 mg
- Organophosphate poisoning: 1.2–2.4 mg IV, doubled every 5 min until the chest is clear and the heart rate is over 80/min
- Children: 0.02 mg/kg (minimum 0.1 mg)
- Ampoule 0.6 mg/mL

## Adverse effects
- Dry mouth, flushing, hot dry skin, fever (especially children)
- Tachycardia, blurred vision, urinary retention, constipation
- Confusion, delirium in the elderly ('mad as a hatter, red as a beet, dry as a bone, blind as a bat, hot as a hare')
- Doses under 0.5 mg in adults can cause paradoxical bradycardia

## Contraindications
- Angle-closure glaucoma, obstructive uropathy, paralytic ileus, myasthenia gravis (relative), tachyarrhythmias
- No absolute contraindication in life-threatening bradycardia or poisoning

## Drug interactions
- Other anticholinergics (TCAs, first-generation antihistamines, phenothiazines): additive effects

## Monitoring
- Heart rate, BP, ECG

## Pregnancy & lactation
Crosses the placenta; use when needed in emergencies.

## Viva points
- Vasovagal attack during a procedure: lie flat, legs up; atropine if bradycardia persists
- Minimum dose 0.5 mg in adults to avoid paradoxical bradycardia
- Signs of atropine toxicity (anticholinergic toxidrome)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.58 (vasovagal reactions); ACLS/resuscitation guidelines. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
